# Full Moon Werewolf

A Skill Harbor house build: Werewolf, the social deduction classic, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. The game is asynchronous on purpose. There is no live session and nobody has to be online at the same time; each phase runs against an announced deadline, so a round takes hours and a game stretches over days, around real life. It plays with 5 to 12 players: hidden werewolves, a seer, plain villagers, a hunter from 8 players, and a witch from 11.

Your assistant is the referee, and refereeing is the whole design. Every role is drawn at random and written immediately into a sealed state file that only the referee holds. Roles are dealt one by one in private 1:1 messages, never in the group thread. At night, the wolves choose their victim by private votes that the referee relays between them (a persistent disagreement is settled by a recorded draw, so the referee never picks a side), and the seer privately probes one player and is answered only "wolf" or "not a wolf". In the morning the referee announces who was eliminated and reveals their role; the village debates in the thread and votes in public; the eliminated player's role is revealed too. A living player's role is never revealed or hinted at, in any message, to anyone. The hunter works by a standing target given privately in advance, so an elimination never stalls the game waiting for someone who is away.

The host can play in their own game. That mode is built in, not improvised: secret messages go...
